{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"On the edge of a quiet harbor stood a little shop filled with maps. Its owner, Mara, had spent years sailing to distant places, but now she preferred helping others plan their journeys. Behind the counter, a brass compass rested beside a jar of smooth beach stones.

One morning, a boy named Eli came in carrying a torn map. He wanted to find the lighthouse on the far side of the bay, he explained, because his grandfather had once taken him there. But the ferry was canceled, and the winding coastal path looked confusing.

Mara spread the map across the counter. Together they traced a route past the old windmill, through a stand of pine trees, and along a sheltered beach. She marked the turns with a blue pencil and packed Eli a small paper bag of biscuits.

“Maps can show you where to go,” she said, “but noticing what’s around you helps you find your way.”

Eli set out beneath a brightening sky. At the windmill, he spotted a painted gull that matched Mara’s drawing. In the pines, he heard waves before he could see them. When he reached the beach, he found a line of flat stones leading toward the lighthouse.

His grandfather was waiting there, smiling in the doorway. They spent the afternoon watching boats cross the bay and sharing biscuits in the shade.

The next day, Eli returned to the map shop with a drawing of his own. He had added the gull, the pine trees, and the trail of stones. Mara pinned it beside the old maps. From then on, whenever someone came looking for a route, she showed them Eli’s picture, too—a reminder that the best journeys leave something worth sharing."}
